annotations.annotation_text: Page 443 opens Book 3, Chapter 2 ("Jaun's Sermon") during the Age of Men phase. This passage continues Jaun (Shaun) preaching to the twenty-nine girls, the Ondt and the Gracehoper fable, departure and farewell, featuring Jaun/Shaun, Issy, the Rainbow Girls. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Liturgical echo "Filius" on page 443 ("Jaun's Sermon"): Catholic ritual, Latin prayer, and sacramental language weave through Jaun (Shaun) preaching to the twenty-nine girls, the Ondt and the Gracehoper fable, departure and farewell. Joyce fuses ecclesiastical solemnity with domestic banality during the Age of Men phase, treating the tavern counter as communion rail and the sleeping body as sacred vessel.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 443 ("Jaun's Sermon"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
